title: Activision Should Hire Former Halo Devs For Next Mainline Game, Former Franchise Director Says
description: Now that development of future Halo games is being handled by Activision Blizzard's hands, some former developers of the series have spoken out to share their thoughts on the shocking but not entirely surprising mix-up. This includes the former franchise creative director, who has provided some salient advice to the Call of Duty publisher. Frank O’Connor has worked on Halo for over 20 years, first working as a writer and community manager before serving as the game's franchise creative director from 2003 to 2023. This is a guy who knows Halo like the back of his hand, and with all that series expertise, he took to LinkedIn on September 25 to share some thoughts on how to make the next Halo great. "Pro-Tip: Do NOT tie it to hardware/services launch cycles, do not try to force it into a shape (or aging platform) that it can't fit and do NOT abandon sandbox," O’Connor said in response to Xbox's former social media manager, Genevieve Harrison, who was pontificating on Activision Blizzard's development tactics. "Pro-Pro-Tip: Hire Bungie, Halo Studios and other laid-off folk who are bursting w. talent and ideas that got nerfed or shut down over the years." In laying out these tips, O’Connor gave three ways the next Halo game could bring the franchise back to its former glory. The first is a "classic" Halo game that focuses on a sandbox, movement, and shooter experience. It'd be "tailored to a core audience [and] scaled to be successful with that core audience and attractive to a broader one so it can grow." A second option could be "something new [and] modern" that reinvents the game. O’Connor suggests this "surprising but fantastic" reinvention could be an action-sandbox game that's a "new take" on the FPS or an "action RPG" that's fundamentally different, but its success comes from a strong story and IP use. Lastly, O’Connor thinks that an Activision Blizzard-esque Halo game could be viable. It could be a sandbox game with "player, progression, and business models" that the publisher is well-known for with the likes of CoD. Given that experience, maybe this idea could be "a big annual or semi-annual spectacle" with consistent content. O’Connor couched these ideas, saying that none of them are "easy, guaranteed, or necessarily viable." Still, he believes that one "could be successful" now that Activision is driving the Warthog. O’Connor isn't the only former developer who shares his opinion on the CoD publisher taking over the Halo reins. Co-creator Marcus Lehto also weighed in, saying on September 23 that he is "shocked but not entirely surprised" by the move. Like Lehto, we're all "eager to learn more about what’s next," and for right now, all we know thus far is that the next Halo game will be a "full-feature, mainline installment" in the long-running series.

title: Xbox Disc-To-Digital Program Is Officially Live For Everyone
description: Following an initial rollout to Xbox Insiders, the Xbox disc-to-digital program is officially available for all Xbox One and Xbox Series X users. The program allows you to receive digital licenses for a whole bunch (but not all) of your physical Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S games, and Microsoft has outlined how it works and a pretty neat trick you can use. In order to claim your digital license for a supported Xbox game, all you need to do is put it into an Xbox console while you're signed in. You'll get a notification to let you know you've received a license. One cool thing is this can be an Xbox Series X or an Xbox One console, even if you're exclusively claiming Xbox Series X games. https://twitter.com/xbox/status/2105040959192916253?s=46 While the disc will also automatically start installing when you insert it, you can turn this feature off by going to the Profile & system section in the settings, then Devices & connections. You'll see an option for Disc and you can uncheck "Play disc automatically." This way, you can more quickly claim licenses in bulk. With a disc inserted using this method, you'll have to manually select the game card on the home screen, select it with the Menu button, and then claim the digital license. Once that's done, you just eject the game and move on to the next one. When you've finished the process, re-check that "Play disc automatically" box for whenever you get your next physical game to play. If your license isn't available to claim, there's a good chance the publisher doesn't support the program. Major companies like Square Enix and Ubisoft don't appear to support it yet, which could limit its usefulness for those who want to truly digitize their entire collection. Once you've claimed the digital license, you should still be able to lend the physical game to a friend, but they will then get the digital license. If they give the disc back to you, you'll receive the license back after re-inserting the game into your own system.

title: Ex-PlayStation Boss Has Some Advice For Xbox: “Pick A Lane”
description: Xbox has undergone major changes since a new leadership team took over. Under Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, Microsoft's gaming division has had waves of mass layoffs, parted ways with several studios, and consolidated its remaining developers under Activision, Blizzard, King, and Bethesda. All of this is being done to make Xbox a profitable part of the Microsoft empire and to grow its reach, but former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden has suggested that the company should "pick a lane" and narrow its focus. "I said in another interview a couple of months ago, you've got to pick a lane," Layden said to The Expansion Pass when he was asked if he had any advice for Sharma. "Either you're going to be a platform competitive with PlayStation--which Xbox has not been competitive with PlayStation for years--but that's not out of the window. You can still make another run at it. And there are certain decisions you have to make around that about the platform. We talked about exclusivity. We talked about how do you incentivize third parties to support your platform in a meaningful way. These are all things around the platform business, or you sit back and realize you are the biggest game publisher in the world--maybe Tencent's bigger--but in the Western world you are the biggest game publisher out there with Activision, Blizzard, Bethesda, and all the other pieces." "Be that. This is your Dreamcast moment. When Sega decided, 'We're just going to be on PlayStation 2 and we're going to get out of the hardware business and just be a great software company. It can be done. It has been done before. That's my advice. Pick a lane." https://youtu.be/rUwPH-s8TVw?si=C6Y_AOa7-ByyOQ5N The "Dreamcast moment" that Layden refers to is the rise and fall of Sega's last home console--the moment when Sega realised it could no longer compete in the gaming hardware market and had to shift entirely to software. Microsoft has been notoriously secretive with the sales of its Xbox hardware, as it's believed that it trails far behind Sony's PlayStation 5 (95.3 million units sold as of June 2026). The future doesn't look too good for Xbox console sales either, as analysts predict that only 2.5 million Xbox Series X|S units will be sold in 2026, as Microsoft prepares for a "rapid wind-down toward zero" ahead of its next-gen console launch. Would it make sense for Xbox to shift towards being a software-only company then? There's certainly evidence to suggest that it might be a viable path forward, as several of its first-party games have done very good numbers on PC and PS5, and if it's streamlining operations to focus on hit franchises like Fallout and Forza Horizon, there is an audience for those games. Of course, releasing games on PlayStation and Steam also means that Xbox has to give up a cut of its revenue, whereas it gets to keep 100% of first-party game sales when they're sold through Xbox console and PC storefronts. Microsoft also charges a fee to third-party developers, so there's a lot of nuance behind the math of sticking with gaming hardware or focusing purely on software.

title: This New Riftbound Card Is An Exciting Variant Of A Time-Traveling Legend
description: While it already feels like it's been around forever, October 31 will mark the one-year anniversary of Riftbound, the trading card game based on Riot Games's popular League of Legends franchise, releasing in Western markets. The game has seen four set releases so far, but there's one more on the schedule, Radiance, before we hit that one-year milestone. There are many exciting cards being revealed as we get closer to Radiance's October 23 launch, and today, we have an exclusive look at the Overnumbered variants of one of the set's most notable names. We've seen the card's base form before, but this new art is a beauty to behold. Without further ado, here's the Overnumbered variants for Ekko, Boy Who Shattered Time. Ekko, Boy Who Shattered Time (Legend - Ekko) Colors: Fury/Mind (Red/Blue) Empower: Exhaust 1 rune and Ekko to empower him Disempower Ekko and exhaust him to reduce the cost of the next unit you play this turn by 2 and a recycled rune of any color and give that unit "Kill me at end of turn." Ekko is known for his ability to bend time to his will, while also creating temporary clones of himself to confuse opponents. With this new card, he can effectively give that ability to other units in your deck, though they will be sent to the discard pile at the end of the turn. Building a deck around this legend will capitalize on cards who can make an immediate impact on the board, like units with Accelerate who enter ready and can attack immediately. Considering that Accelerate costs are one exhausted rune and one recycled rune, Ekko's discount means you'll still pay less to summon the Accelerated unit. Radiance, Riftbound's fifth major set, launches October 23 in local game stores and big-box retailers. Prerelease events, or "Pre-Rifts" as they're known in Riftbound, will be held at local game stores beginning October 16.

title: The Witcher 3 Is Having A Record-Breaking Comeback In A Very Busy Gaming Month
description: More than a decade has passed since The Witcher 3: The Wild Hunt first launched, and on Steam, the game is doing better than ever. With the launch of The Witcher 3 Remastered, the game has surged up the Steam charts and has reached its best concurrent players level--ever. At the time of writing, the CCU has peaked at 120,975 players, beating the previous January 2020 record of 103,329 players. That older milestone was reached after The Witcher TV series launched on Netflix, but the new numbers have blown it out of the water. The game is also available through other PC storefronts like GOG and the Epic Games Store, as well as on PS5, Switch 2, and Xbox Series X|S, so it's likely that the total number of players is much higher. Clearly, there's still a lot people out there who are more than happy to toss a coin to their Witcher. https://twitter.com/thewitcher/status/2104959102858178595 The Remastered Edition of The Witcher 3 is a big one, as it added numerous technical and graphical improvements to the original 2015 game. What makes this even more impressive is that the game is reaching these player numbers at a very busy time on the gaming calendar, as numerous high-profile games have launched in an effort to avoid being caught up in the wake of GTA 6's November release. Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Control Resonant, Marvel's Wolverine, and Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave all landed within weeks of each other, and that's not including the live-service games which regularly dominate the charts. One other thing worth noting is that The Witcher 3 Remastered is a free upgrade to anyone who already owns the game. Considering that it has lifetime sales of 65 million units globally (as of May 2026) and has been regularly discounted, it's likely that plenty of existing owners of The Witcher 3 dived back into the game to see all the new improvements. If you're wondering if the download juice is worth the squeeze, you can check out GameSpot’s in-depth breakdown of what’s new in the remaster to see all the changes for yourself. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_oEdB5S2d3U Beyond a return to the Continent, Witcher fans have much to look forward to. The Witcher 3 is getting a new expansion in 2027, Songs of the Past, and The Witcher 4 could be out as soon as 2028. CD Projekt Red is rumored to be working on a multiplayer Witcher game, and the company recently confirmed that it is working with Scopely on a new mobile game based on one of its franchises--which could be The Witcher or Cyberpunk.

title: Steam Is Finally Changing How Games Get Their Big Front-Page Break
description: The front page of Steam has long been a hot commodity for game developers and publishers, but next year, some big changes are coming. Valve has announced that it'll be changing how it handles game discoverability during sales and promotions on Steam, as it'll be moving away from the old model of a tightly controlled page through a manually curated calendar to dynamic, personalized recommendations that'll cater to individual user preferences and their purchase history. Historically, Valve employees selected which games got featured in a limited number of fixed slots on the Steam front page, and only a fraction of discounted games got valuable front-page visibility. According to Valve, preliminary experiments resulted in up to 10 times as many games appearing per day in the Discounts & Events section, leading to measurable increases in store page visits and wishlist additions. Steam deals pageWhat does this mean? For developers, it means that they won't need to rely on relationships, manual pitches, or sheer luck to potentially get a front-page placement. This will also effectively level the playing field for all developers, as smaller teams and publishers typically don't have the budget to compete with AAA blockbuster marketing teams. Valve added that it has already paused scheduling curated placements in the Weekend Deals, Midweek Deals, and Daily Deals sections, and it will soon roll out new and updated tools to help developers better manage their discounts and sale events on Steam. "Our goal is to let developers focus on crafting the most compelling games and deals for customers, and not spend time trying to convince someone at Valve to feature their products," Valve wrote. The rollout window for this change to the Steam storefront will be in early 2027. This news comes on the eve of a new Steam sales event, as the week-long Steam Autumn Sale kicks off on October 1. There'll also be a new Next Fest held at the end of October, while themed events for the rest of 2026 include Steam Scream V Fest, Auto-Battler RPG Fest, and Cooking Fest before the Steam Winter Sale in December.

title: The Biggest New Game Releases Of October 2026
description: If you thought September was a big month for new releases, then you ain't seen nothing yet. As the days tick down to the November launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, numerous games are looking to avoid being caught in the blast radius of the year's biggest release, which has led to an absolutely stacked October. Between original releases, sequels, and hot indie games, the next couple of weeks are loaded with options across a wide variety of genres and ideas. You can check out our top picks below, and if you want to see what's closing out the year, you can also read through our list of upcoming 2026 games. Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UTVVw9fsHVA&pp=ygUvRHluYXN0eSBXYXJyaW9ycyAzOiBDb21wbGV0ZSBFZGl0aW9uIFJlbWFzdGVyZWQ%3D Release date: October 1 Platforms: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2 We're suckers for a good Dynasty Warriors game, as these one-against-too-damn-many-enemies simulators are perfect for when you want to turn your brain off and revel in being a battlefield badass. There have been many games in the series over the years, and Dynasty Warriors 3 is often considered a high point for the series, as it further refined its musou formula. If you've never played it, you can grab this new remaster, which enhances the original with Unreal Engine 5 graphics, numerous gameplay tweaks, and plenty of cannon-fodder troops to mow down. Ghost of Yotei: Complete Edition https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2bQrrWCRkMY&pp=ygUgR2hvc3Qgb2YgWW90ZWk6IENvbXBsZXRlIEVkaXRpb24%3D Release date: October 1 Platforms: PS5 Ghost of Yotei fans can look forward to a whole lot of new content for the game--like the new narrative expansion Echoes of Sekigahara and the new combat-survival mode--but if you haven't played it yet, now is a fine time to grab the game's Complete Edition. This $70 version of the game gets you all of that new content, as well as the base game, the online co-op mode Ghost of Yotei Legends, and all of the Digital Deluxe Edition content. Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n5irVTl0mD8 Release date: October 2 Platforms: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S In the mood to take a trip to the danger zone? You can do just that in Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, Bandai Namco's long-running aerial-action series. This new entry in the franchise will let you take to the skies to participate in dogfights, eliminate threats, and rise through the ranks to earn your wings. Developer Project Aces has done its homework to push the series to new heights with Wings of Theve, and when you're not in the cockpit, there's a first-person story mode to experience. Aion 2 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vZV1pQP09p8&pp=ygUGQWlvbiAy Release date: October 5 Platforms: PC Aion 2 wants to be the one game where the sky isn't the limit, as Developer NCSoft has made verticality a key part of the MMORPG. Built on Unreal Engine 5 across a world that NCSoft says is up to 36 times bigger than the original Aion, combat is built around seamlessly chaining skills--on or above the ground--adapting to encounters, and using precision timing to triumph. The game also looks visually stunning thanks to its Unreal Engine 5 visuals, and you can expect to dive into over 200 dungeons after you're done spending a few hours in the highly detailed character creator. Gears of War: E-day https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SRFE0gCsgLg Release date: October 6 Platforms: PC, Xbox Series X|S After seven years, Gears of War is back and ready to tell the story of humanity's first, disastrous encounter with the Locust. So far, it looks like the campaign will harken back to the horror-inspired roots of the first game as you fight through several days of hell, using an arsenal of classic weapons and completely overhauled gameplay mechanics. Multiplayer is where Gears of War: E-day looks like it'll really shine, as alongside classic PvP, the new Horde Siege mode looks like a playground for creating unique stories as teams fight against the odds to accomplish various objectives and at least one Smash Mouth-inspired Achievement. Star Wars: Galactic Racer https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=acy2Cixyya0 Release date: October 6 Platforms: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S We've had several Star Wars racing games in the past, but Star Wars: Galactic Racer looks like it'll stand out from the pack by cribbing a few ideas from successful genres and throwing in some Burnout influences for good measure. Developer Fuse Games is aiming to evolve the racing-game genre by fusing roguelite progression and replayability with high-speed competition, while also showing what the citizens get up to for fun when they're not dealing with warring empires on a daily basis. Just remember: Sebulba did nothing wrong. Hellraiser: Revival https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xEOr2w8moTg Release date: October 8 Platforms: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2 In a welcome change of pace, a cult-classic horror franchise from the '80s and '90s is getting a video game adaptation, and it's not an asynchronous multiplayer title. Instead, Hellraiser: Revival looks and plays like a very horny Resident Evil, as you're thrown into a struggle for survival against Pinhead and his Cenobite goons--and all in the name of love. Saber Interactive has been promising a fresh spin on Clive Barker's books and film adaptations that is designed to make you feel uncomfortable--one that holds nothing back and isn't afraid to create a realm of pure, gory torment. No tears please! It's a waste of good suffering. Silver Pines https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sfN4uMZK0Cw&pp=ygUMU2lsdmVyIFBpbmVz Release date: October 8 Platforms: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, Switch Time for some horror, and Silver Pines looks like an intriguing new game to check out if you're looking for some metroidvania-inspired suspense. Billed as a love letter to classic survival-horror games, Silver Pines follows an investigator caught up in a dark web of intrigue as they have to slug it out with the terror lurking in a small town and solve the puzzles blocking their progress. The game oozes atmosphere with its eye-catching art direction, and you'll also need to carefully manage your scarce resources as the darkness creeps up on you. Legion Was Here https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OqVxHCm0JHg&pp=ygUPTGVnaW9uIFdhcyBIZXJl Release date: October 13 Platforms: PC What's the coolest part of the Mission: Impossible movies? Contrary to popular belief, it's not watching Tom Cruise tempt fate with a risky stunt, but those glorious disguises. Legion Was Here captures that charm, as you'll need to use your skills to steal faces and impersonate dangerous individuals to survive deadly conversations in this dark-comedy spy deduction game. If you're the kind of person who spends far too long in the character-creation part of games, then you'll get a kick out of Legion Was Here. Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B6Snuv1BMjE Release date: October 9 Platforms: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2 In case you thought Capcom was done after releasing four big games this year, think again. Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen is an expanded version of the sequel, featuring a new region to explore and enhanced gameplay. Set in the long-abandoned region of Norgan, players will join forces with the enigmatic Eir and journey to unravel the secrets of the undying Fallen Dragon. Valor Mortis https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PvpxF8upFQM Release date: October 13 Platforms: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S Your typical soulslike is a third-person adventure, but can shifting to first-person shake up that formula? That's an interesting premise from Ghostrunner developer One More Level, as the studio is reimagining the Napoleonic Wars through a lens of challenging combat and mutated soldiers who'd look right at home in a Resident Evil game if it took place during the Battle of Waterloo. One other ace that the game has up its sleeve is its price; as compared to the other $70 releases coming this month, Valor Mortis will set you back just $40, and it's a day-one Game Pass title. Planet Zoo 2 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fnw_niw9nzQ&pp=ygUMUGxhbmV0IFpvbyAy Release date: October 13 Platforms: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S The first Planet Zoo game tasked players with building a planet-sized sanctuary for all creatures big and small, and the sequel looks like it'll expand considerably on that idea. Even more tools will be at your disposal to help with your conservationist creativity, and the game's menagerie will include new aquatic and flying species. Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Qkg4CpTRugE&pp=ygUad2FyaGFtbWVyIDQwIDAwMCBib2x0Z3VuIDI%3D Release date: October 14 Platforms: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S The first Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun game was a fun throwback to the past with its boomer-shooter design, and it looks like Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 isn't straying far from that established formula. More guns and more enemies to turn into pixelated giblets sounds like a fun time, and to seal the deal on its heavy metal influences, the game even features a musical cameo by none other than Doom 2016 and Doom Eternal composer Mick Gordon. The sequel is slightly switching things up, as you can choose to play as either Ultramarine Malum Caedo or Battle Sister Nyra Veyrath when you take on the daemonic demigod Vashtorr and hordes of enemies from the Warp. Over the Hill https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TRwRd-RfrwI&pp=ygUVT3ZlciB0aGUgSGlsbCB0cmFpbGVy Release date: October 14 Platforms: PC If you enjoyed cozy racing games like Art of Rally and Absolute Drift, then you'll want to check out Over the Hill from Funselektor Labs. This time, the focus is on the golden age of offroading, as you'll need to guide your trusty all-terrain vehicle to its final destination. If you don't feel like tackling challenging trails on your own, the game features a co-op mode for friends to join you for a few sessions of scenic minimalism. The Witch's Bakery https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6xRCu4qaPhI&pp=ygUSdGhlIHdpdGNoJ3MgYmFrZXJ5 Release date: October 14 Platforms: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, Switch What's better than a fresh loaf of bread from a French baker? A fresh loaf of bread from a French baker who also happens to be a witch, that's what. The Witch's Bakery is a 2D narrative adventure where you'll get to serve up delicious baked treats, but also use your baking skills to heal the hearts of local Parisians. Each day is split into three phases, where you'll get to work, explore, and hone your magic. But more importantly, are you going to finish that croissant? Castlevania: Belmont's Curse https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hisx60NSqtY Release date: October 15 Platforms: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch Gears of War isn't the only big franchise making a comeback after a years-long absence, as Castlevania is once again cracking its whip this month. Set in a version of Paris that has seen better days before Dracula transformed the French capital into a monster-infested hellscape, this new entry in the series has been developed by the Rogue Prince of Persia studio Evil Empire. It looks like classic Castlevania, with the 2.5D approach that Evil Empire has taken, as you'll be battling all manner of monsters, fallen French legends, and more on your journey to take down Dracula. Heck, it's even a Netflix reunion of voice actors from the Castlevania animated series. Enshrouded https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_6atVNfcECU&pp=ygUKRW5zaHJvdWRlZA%3D%3D Release date: October 15 Platforms: PC, PS5 The early-access journey of Enshrouded comes to an end soon, as the game's official 1.0 release hits PC and consoles on October 15. In case you missed it when it was first announced, Enshrouded draws inspiration from games like Valheim and Minecraft, giving you all the tools you need to survive and thrive in a fantasy world. You've got everything you could ask for to easily build a kingdom, or if that doesn't appeal to you, you can drop the hammer and pick up a sword for some adventuring fun instead. Bluey's Happy Snaps https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MpX7Ogr39zw&pp=ygUTQmx1ZXkncyBIYXBweSBTbmFwcw%3D%3D Release date: October 15 Platforms: PC, PS5, PS4, Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, Switch 2, Switch New Bluey games have been arriving at a steady clip lately, with the latest titled Bluey's Happy Snaps. This time, it's up to you to take the adorable Bluey and Bingo to new locations and start shooting--with a camera, you weirdo. You can visit familiar spots from the show, and use your snaps to create your own scrapbook of memories when you're done. Stupid Never Dies https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k_33MQFuVEY&pp=ygURU3R1cGlkIE5ldmVyIERpZXM%3D Release date: October 22 Platforms: PC It's going to take a lot of effort to stand out in October, but Stupid Never Dies might have that magic sauce thanks to a weird title, imaginative visuals, and plenty of gameplay to sink your teeth into. As the weakest zombie alive, Davy, it's up to you to power up the lovestruck hero by defeating the mysterious KOM, recovering humanity's lost knowledge, and surviving the deadly depths of an interdimensional dungeon. The debut game from GPTrack50, Stupid Never Dies is all about eat-or-be-eaten action, as Davy can munch enemies to steal their powers, replace his body parts with powerful tech, and unleash his imagination to transform reality. Final Fantasy Resonance https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QD0MUx40l6c&t=57s&pp=0gcJCS8MAYcqIYzv Release date: October 22 Platforms: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, Switch 1997 marked the start of a new 3D era for Final Fantasy, but what if the franchise stuck to its 2D roots? That's the question that Final Fantasy Resonance aims to answer, as it revives a dead mobile game and transforms it into a HD-2D adventure. What might make this one special is how the original story features several famous faces from across the Final Fantasy franchise as "Visions" that can join you in battle, ranging from Final Fantasy 6's Terra to Final Fantasy 16's Clive Rosfield. The game also looks gorgeous--as you'd expect from an engine used to power titles like Octopath Traveler--and it has received various enhancements like voice acting and overhauled battle systems to make it play like a traditional RPG. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FZmCtpTSI4E&pp=ygUdTmludGVuZG8gU3dpdGNoIFNwb3J0cyBSZXNvcnQ%3D Release date: October 22 Platforms: Switch 2 Nintendo's sports games are a fun way to keep your body moving, and in Nintendo Switch Sports Resort, you can take part in a wide variety of activities. Both single-player and co-op multiplayer will be offered, and the sports included for your trip to Wuhu Island range from archery and tennis to some extreme activities like skateboarding and table tennis. The real star of the show is thumb wrestling, as after you've declared a thumb war, you can use the Joy-Con 2 controller to move your mighty digit to victory. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a1usju9Bjo4 Release date: October 23 Platforms: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, Switch The year just wouldn't feel right without some Call of Duty in the mix, and 2026's entry in the blockbuster series is all about Modern Warfare once again. If you've played any Call of Duty games in the last 20 years, you know to expect a weekend-warrior campaign, this time with a conflict involving North Korea and an evil Mads Mikkelsen, plenty of multiplayer action, and an extraction shooter experience in DMZ. What you shouldn't expect is a day-one launch on Xbox Game Pass this year, as Call of Duty is returning to its premium roots. Xbox gamers can still get an exclusive perk, as well as a heck of a cool weapon blueprint as a preorder bonus. Emberville https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hPsCEHnjBJc&pp=ygUKRW1iZXJ2aWxsZQ%3D%3D Release date: October 27 Platforms: PC Emberville has been in development since 2023, and if you've been looking for a blend of Stardew Valley-like farming and Diablo-flavored combat, this might be just the game for you. The action-adventure RPG features the voice talents of the Witcher himself, Doug Cockle, and Alex Jordan, who voiced multiple versions of the character Dolski in The Alters. The game also features a two-button system for combat that has plenty of depth, as well as a leveling system that allows you to experiment with classes and abilities. Phantom Blade Zero https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WCClGv4MNDA Release date: October 29 Platforms: PC, PS5 Action-game fans have been eating well throughout 2026, and we hope you saved room for a side of Phantom Blade Zero. Another action-RPG inspired by Chinese mythology, folklore, and horror, Phantom Blade Zero is all about mastering fast-paced combat in a dark fantasy semi-open world. Featuring martial arts inspired by the Golden Age of Hong Kong action films--and overseen by the legendary Donnie Yen--the game follows an assassin named Soul, who only has 66 days left to live and stylishly exact his revenge.

title: Alleged WoW: Forever Survey Teases 11 New Classes, Including Some Deep Cuts
description: World of Warcraft: Forever's new take on classic Azeroth is opening the door to all kinds of new ideas in the old-school version of Blizzard's MMORPG, and new classes look to be one of them. Blizzard, of course, has added a total of four new classes over the last two decades to the modern version of WoW: Death Knight, Monk, Demon Hunter, and Evoker. But an alleged leaked survey pushed to select WoW players via Blizzard's Battle.net launcher is now asking about potential new classes for WoW: Forever, the recently revealed third version of the MMO that will introduce new quests, zones, and content to the "vanilla" version of WoW. It's not the first time Blizzard has conducted a survey this way, and while Blizzard asks participants not to disclose the survey's details, their contents almost always find their way online. That's the case here, as players were quick to share information about 11 potential new classes listed in the survey, and content creators like Bellular have gone as far as to provide a full breakdown. Information contained about each of these potential classes includes basic lore, what types of weapons they would be able to use, the armor class they would wear, the resources they would use, what roles they would fill, and even signature abilities. The classes listed in the survery are: Bard Death Knight Demon Hunter Illusionist Monk Necromancer Metalborn/Runemaster/Runeknight San'layn Tinker Warden Witch Three of the new classes would essentially be "new," old-school versions of existing WoW classes like Demon Hunter, Monk, and Death Knight. Considering how fast-paced classes like Monk and Demon Hunter are in the modern version of the game, their Forever counterparts would likely feel significantly different. It's the eight "new" classes that are the most exciting, however. Some of these are ideas that have existed in WoW lore for ages or ones that Blizzard even originally toyed with during the game's early development. The Tinker, for example, is a class many expect to come to the modern version of WoW at some point but is listed in the survey. They would be the ultimate engineer, capable of using mech suits and gadgets to tank, deal damage, and support other players. Another potential class, the Necromancer, was an idea Blizzard originally had planned for vanilla WoW, only for it to eventually be scrapped. In Forever, Blizzard is proposing a version of the class that seems like it's taking some inspiration from Diablo 2's class of the same name, with abilities like Bone Spear and Corpse Explosion. The survey additionally lists the San'layn, a group of vampires who broke free of the Lich King's domination. This class seems like it would lean fully into the vampire fantasy, with a number of blood-based abilities that could make them similar to retail WoW's Blood Death Knight specialization. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zerqLHQPN9Y Two other classes steeped in WoW lore proposed in the survey are the Warden and Runemaster. Wardens are the iconic Night Elf faction famous for hunting down and imprisoning Azeroth's greatest threats. How exactly that would work when it comes to Horde players is unclear, but the survey notes that the Wardens would open their ranks "out of necessity" in order to deal with greater threats. Runemasters, on the other hand, are beings infused with power by the Titans who use a rune system that sounds similar to that of modern WoW's Death Knights to heal and fight. That rune system itself was originally for an early version of the Runemaster class that was later scrapped and its core mechanic repurposed. This class appears to have been listed by multiple different names in various versions of the survey, also appearing by the name Metalborn and Runeknight. Other classes seem almost entirely new. The survey lists classes like Bard, Witch, and Illusionist among potential additions. The Bard sounds about like what you would expect, a healer and support class capable of buffing allies, while the Witch and Illusionists are two new flavors of spellcasters. Illusionists would summon and conjure creatures and objects to aid them in battle, while the Witch uses dark powers like blood rituals and even the power of the old gods to buff allies and destroy their foes. Whether or not any or all of these potential new classes will eventually make their way into Forever remains to be seen, but Blizzard does have, well, forever to make them a reality. In the meantime there's plenty new for WoW: Forever players to discover, including over 1,000 new quests, four new zones, an account-wide Legacy perk system, and more. WoW: Forever's beta is currently live until October 21, with Forever's full launch set for November 4.

title: GTA 6 Won’t Spoof Disney World, And That’s Too Bad
description: GTA 6 will not include its own spoof on one of Florida's most iconic venues: Walt Disney World. I adore all things Disney, including the parks. But I also appreciate and enjoy Rockstar's penchant for sarcasm and making fun of things. And Disney World? There is a lot to poke fun at. So I am a bit bummed that Walt Disney World--or whatever Rockstar would name its simulacrum--won't appear in GTA 6. Game Informer asked Rockstar if Florida's central region, including Orlando and its tourist destinations like Walt Disney World and Universal Studios, would be represented in GTA 6 in some form, and Jack McPherson said they wouldn't. However, McPherson stressed that GTA 6 will offer the "full Florida experience" in numerous other ways. “We have to constantly evaluate the diversity of landscapes, towns, structures, landmarks, vistas, plant species, rock formations and everything else before we work with design and narrative to distill a list down that best works with and serves the game’s needs. So, while we may not have those exact locations, everything we have is geared to getting that full Florida experience!” Lucia and Jason in GTA 6.GTA 6 also won't feature SeaWorld or Florida's iconic "Space Coast," featuring Cape Canaveral's historic launch pad. I am not too surprised by any of this, though, considering GTA 6 takes place in Vice City, a stand-in for Miami, which is a four-hour, 230-mile drive from Orlando. I know GTA 6 is going to be a big game--featuring the biggest game map Rockstar ever made--but I never expected the map to run all the way up to Orlando. Jay Klaitz, who famously portrayed Lester in Grand Theft Auto 5, previously said in an interview that he wondered if Rockstar would create its own, legally distinct version of Disney World that could be called “Psycho Park.” “That would be interesting too if they sort of delve into that environment,” he said. While GTA 6 might not feature its own take on Disney World, it's possible the park could be referenced in GTA 6's radio chatter, and some spoofs could come there. The well runs deep for things Rockstar can make fun of Disney World for, including its ever-increasing ticket prices, the price to buy literally anything in the parks, and the so-called Disney Adult phenomenon, just to name a few options. I love Disney, but even the most diehard fans have their issues. As it happens, the last game in the series, GTA 5, was set where Disneyland--the OG Disney park--is located in the Los Angeles area, and that game also did not feature its own theme park spoof that players could visit. However, GTA 5 featured a film production company known as Fred's Pictures, which was an obvious reference to Disney. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
